title: Introduce mini-batch variance emulator and hotpath cataloger reporter
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: We need a compact, deterministic way to inject micro-variance into mini-batch scheduling and measure kernel affinity impact across short-lived bursts. This PR adds a lightweight mini-batch variance emulator (python) that can replay controlled burst patterns and per-sequence timing jitter, plus a Go-based hotpath cataloger reporter that consumes synthesized traces and emits compact kernel-affinity maps and a per-kernel tail heatmap. Key goals: reproducible microburst injection, low-overhead instrumentation, pluggable exporter interface, and a small reporter payload that feeds downstream visualization and regression detectors. Implementation summary: 1) bench/emulators/mini_batch_variance_emulator.py: deterministic RNG seed, pluggable sequence mix, per-request latency jitter model, and an orchestrator that emits synthetic trace lines compatible with our bench trace format. 2) bench/reporters/hotpath_cataloger/main.go: streaming parser that groups traces into hotpath candidates, computes kernel affinity histograms, coalesces short-lived hot intervals, and writes compact NDJSON records with metadata. 3) bench/tests/test_variance_emulator.py and bench/tests/test_cataloger_integration.py: unit+integration harnesses that run in CI with a small fixture dataset. 4) docs/benchmark-runbook.md: runbook describing how to run the emulator against a real cluster and interpret the cataloger output. How it differs from existing tools: existing suite focuses on long-lived session replay and coarse quantiles. This PR intentionally targets microburst patterns (10-200ms span) and provides a first-class compact artifact — kernel-affinity maps — that are both human-readable and machine-consumable for automated regression detection. Backwards compatibility: the emulator outputs the legacy bench trace header so existing downstream consumers can opt-in. The cataloger introduces a new minimal NDJSON schema version (v1) and includes a compatibility flag to emit legacy hist summaries. How to run locally: python bench/emulators/mini_batch_variance_emulator.py --seed 42 --profile microburst-10-50 --out ./tmp/trace.log && go run bench/reporters/hotpath_cataloger/main.go --input ./tmp/trace.log --out ./tmp/catalog.ndjson Evaluation note: on a small G4 test cluster we reproduced a previously-observed p99 amplification (1.6x) when injecting 3x variance in per-sequence timing; the cataloger correctly surfaced the dominant kernel group and returned a concise affinity map that matched perf sampling. Checklist: - [x] deterministic emulator core - [x] parser + cataloger - [x] tests and CI - [x] docs/runbook - [x] small fixture to reproduce p99 spike Limitations and follow-ups: the current emulator is single-node and synthetic load does not emulate multi-tenant interference; follow-up tickets are suggested for cross-node wavefront coordination and a visualization plugin for the console. Related: ENG-5213 (microburst debug), ENG-5240 (cataloger integration).

Maya Patel: Addressed both nits; added context propagation and switched default log level to info.

release_notes: Add a mini-batch variance emulator and hotpath cataloger to benchmark-lab. Provides deterministic microburst injection and compact kernel-affinity artifacts to help diagnose short-span p95/p99 amplifications. No breaking changes.
notes_for_operators: When running against a production-like cluster, start with --profile microburst-10-50 and inspect catalog.ndjson via tools/catviewer. The NDJSON schema includes a version field; validators in bench/reporters will reject unknown versions by default to prevent accidental ingestion.
ci_summary: Initial run had a flake in TestCatalogerIntegration (timeout). Added deterministic fixtures and retry; subsequent CI run passed on linux/amd64 and macos/arm64 jobs. Lint and vet passed.
security_considerations: No new network endpoints. Cataloger reads local trace files; ensure traces containing PII are redacted before running. The emulator supports a redact mode (see runbook).
